p.src: The story goes that Wu the Scholar said, “I have thought of three men whose hearts are filled with honor, whose martial skills are outstanding, and who would brave boiling water and fire, sharing life and death with us. Only by securing these three men can we accomplish this undertaking.” Chao Gai asked, “What sort of men are these three? What are their names? Where do they live?” Wu Yong replied, “They are three brothers who live in Shijie Village beside the Liangshan Marsh in Jizhou. They ordinarily make their living by fishing, though they have also engaged in illicit trading on the marsh. Their surname is Ruan. The eldest is called Ruan Xiao'er, ‘The Year-God Who Stands His Ground’; the second is Ruan Xiaowu, ‘The Short-Lived Second Son’; and the third is Ruan Xiaoqi, ‘The Living King of Hell.’ The three are blood brothers. Years ago, I lived there for several years and became acquainted with them. Though they are illiterate men, I saw that they dealt with others in a truly honorable spirit and were fine fellows, so I kept company with them. It has now been nearly two years since I last saw them. If we can enlist these three, our great enterprise is certain to succeed.” Chao Gai said, “I too have heard the names of the three Ruan brothers, though I have never met them. Shijie Village is no more than a hundred-odd li from here. Why not send someone to invite them here for a discussion?” Wu Yong replied, “If we merely send someone to invite them, why should they agree to come? I must go there myself and use this ever-ready tongue of mine to persuade them to join us.” Chao Gai was delighted. “An excellent plan, Master. When can you leave?” Wu Yong answered, “There is no time to lose. I shall leave at the third watch tonight and can reach the village by noon tomorrow.” Chao Gai said, “Excellent.”

p.src: Ruan Xiao'er came out wearing a tattered headcloth and an old robe, his feet bare. Seeing that it was Wu Yong, he hastily offered a greeting and said, “What brings you here, Professor? What wind has blown you all this way?” Wu Yong replied, “There is a small matter in which I have come especially to seek your help, Second Brother.” Ruan Xiao'er said, “Whatever it is, speak freely.” Wu Yong said, “It has already been two years since I left this place. I now serve as a resident tutor in the household of a wealthy gentleman. He is preparing a banquet and requires more than ten golden carp, each weighing fourteen or fifteen catties, so I have come especially to appeal to you.” Ruan Xiao'er laughed and said, “First share three cups with me, Professor; then we shall talk.” Wu Yong said, “Indeed, part of my purpose in coming was to share three cups with you, Second Brother.” Ruan Xiao'er said, “There are several taverns across the lake. We can pole a boat over.” Wu Yong said, “Excellent. I also wish to say a word to Fifth Brother. Do you know whether he is at home?” Ruan Xiao'er said, “We can go and find him.” The two went to the shore of the marsh, untied one of the little boats moored to a deadwood stake, and Ruan Xiao'er helped Wu Yong aboard. He took a birchwood oar from beside a tree root and poled steadily onward. Soon they had pushed away from shore and headed out onto the lake. As they were going, Ruan Xiao'er suddenly beckoned and called, “Seventh Brother, have you seen Fifth Brother?” Wu Yong looked and saw a boat emerging from among the reeds. What did the man look like? p.src: The two boats followed one another across the lake. Before long, they rowed to a place surrounded entirely by water, where seven or eight thatched cottages stood on a high mound. Ruan Xiao'er called, “Mother, is Fifth Brother here?” The old woman replied, “Do not even mention him! He cannot catch any fish, and he has spent day after day gambling until he has lost every last coin. Just now he took the hairpin from my head and went off to gamble in town.” Ruan Xiao'er laughed and rowed the boat away. From the boat behind, Ruan Xiaoqi said, “Brother, I do not know what is wrong—whenever we gamble, we only lose. What rotten luck! It is not only you who cannot win; I too have lost until I am stripped bare.” Wu Yong thought to himself, “They have fallen into my scheme.” The two boats drew alongside each other and headed toward the market town of Shijie Village. p.src: The three boats now poled into the lotus beds beneath the waterside pavilion, where all three were moored. They helped Scholar Wu ashore and entered the tavern. In the waterside pavilion they selected a red-lacquered table with stools. Ruan Xiao'er said, “Sir, please forgive the coarseness of us three brothers. Teacher, take the seat of honor.” Wu Yong said, “That would never do.” Ruan Xiaoqi said, “Elder Brother, just take the host's seat and let the Teacher sit in the guest's place. We two brothers shall sit down first.” Wu Yong said, “Seventh Brother is as quick-tempered as ever.” When the four were seated, they called for the innkeeper to bring a bucket of wine. The waiter set out four large cups, laid down four pairs of chopsticks, placed four dishes of vegetables, and brought a bucket of wine to set upon the table. Ruan Xiao'er asked, “What have you to eat with the wine?” The waiter replied, “We have just slaughtered a yellow ox, with fine fat meat marbled like a flowered cake.” Ruan Xiao'er said, “Cut us ten catties in large chunks.” Ruan Xiaowu said, “Teacher, do not laugh at us; we have little enough with which to honor you.” Wu Yong said, “It is I who have come to impose upon you and put you to much trouble.” Ruan Xiao'er said, “Do not speak so!” They urged the waiter to keep pouring the wine. Before long the beef had been cut onto two platters and brought to the table. The three Ruan brothers pressed Wu Yong to eat a few pieces, but after that he could eat no more. The other three fell upon the food like wolves and tigers and ate for some time.

p.src: Ruan Xiaowu asked, “Teacher, what important business brings you here?” Ruan Xiao'er said, “The Teacher now tutors in the household of a wealthy gentleman. He has come today because he needs a dozen or more golden carp, each weighing fourteen or fifteen catties, and has sought us out especially.” Ruan Xiaoqi said, “At ordinary times we could get even thirty or fifty, let alone a mere dozen; however many more were wanted, we brothers could undertake to supply them. But just now, even fish weighing ten catties are hard to come by.” Ruan Xiaowu said, “Since the Teacher has come so far, we can at least furnish a dozen or so weighing five or six catties as a gift.” Wu Yong said, “I have plenty of silver with me and will pay whatever the price comes to. Only, smaller ones will not do; they must weigh fourteen or fifteen catties.” Ruan Xiaoqi said, “Teacher, there is nowhere to find them. Even the five- or six-catty fish Fifth Brother promised cannot be had at once; you would have to wait several days. I have a bucket of small live fish in my boat. Let us bring them up to go with the wine.” Ruan Xiaoqi went to his boat and brought up a bucket of small fish weighing some five or seven catties. He took them to the kitchen himself, had them prepared and divided among three plates, then brought them to the table. Ruan Xiaoqi said, “Teacher, please make do with a little of this.”

p.src: The four ate and drank for another while. As the sky gradually darkened, Wu Yong thought, “It will be difficult to talk in this tavern. Tonight I shall surely stay at their house for the time being, and once there I can broach the matter.” Ruan Xiao'er said, “It is late tonight. Teacher, please stay the night at my house, and tomorrow we can discuss what is to be done.” Wu Yong said, “It was no easy matter for me to make this journey, and fortunately I have found you brothers all together today. It is plain that you will not let me repay the cost of this feast. Tonight I shall borrow Second Brother's house for a night's rest. I have a little silver with me, so may I trouble you to buy a jar of wine here, purchase some meat, and find a pair of chickens in the village, that we may all get drunk together tonight?” Ruan Xiao'er said, “Why should the Teacher spend his money? We brothers will arrange everything ourselves; there will be no trouble finding what is needed.” Wu Yong said, “I came here expressly to entertain you three. If you still refuse to humor me, I shall take my leave this very moment.” Ruan Xiaoqi said, “Since the Teacher puts it that way, let us accept his kindness and enjoy the meal; we can settle the rest afterward.” Wu Yong said, “Seventh Brother is indeed forthright and decisive!” Wu Yong took out one tael of silver and handed it to Ruan Xiaoqi, who bought a jar of wine from the proprietor and borrowed a large crock to hold it; they also bought twenty catties of raw and cooked beef and a pair of large chickens. Ruan Xiao'er said, “I shall pay you for my wine as well.” The proprietor said, “Excellent! Excellent!”

p.src: The four left the tavern and went down to the boats again. They put all the wine and meat in the cabins, cast off the mooring ropes, and rowed straight away toward Ruan Xiao'er's house. On reaching the door, they went ashore, moored the boats to the stakes as before, and carried in the wine and meat. All four went around to the rear and sat down, then called for lamps to be lit. Of the three Ruan brothers, only Ruan Xiao'er had a wife and family; neither Ruan Xiaowu nor Ruan Xiaoqi had ever married. The four men settled themselves in the waterside pavilion behind Ruan Xiao'er's house. Ruan Xiaoqi slaughtered the chickens and asked his sister-in-law and the little servant they had hired to prepare them in the kitchen. At about the first watch of the night, all the wine and meat were carried in and set upon the table.

Ruan Xiaoqi slaughtered the chickens and asked his sister-in-law and the little servant they had hired to prepare them in the kitchen.
At about the first watch of the night, all the wine and meat were carried in and set upon the table.

p.src: Wu Yong urged the brothers to drink a few more cups, then brought up the matter of buying fish again. “This is such a large place—how is it that you have no fish of that size?” Ruan the Second said, “To tell you the truth, Professor, fish that large are found only in the Liangshan Marsh. Our Shijie Lake is too small and narrow to hold such great fish.” Wu Yong said, “This place is not far from the Liangshan Marsh, and the same stretch of water connects them. Why do you not go there and catch some?” Ruan the Second heaved a sigh. “Say no more!” Wu Yong asked again, “Second Brother, why do you sigh?” Ruan the Fifth took up the tale. “You do not know, Professor. The Liangshan Marsh used to be the source of our livelihood, but now we dare not go there at all.” Wu Yong said, “In a place so vast, surely the authorities cannot have forbidden fishing.” Ruan the Fifth said, “What authorities would dare forbid us to fish? Even the living King of Hell could not keep us from it!” Wu Yong said, “If the authorities have issued no prohibition, why do you dare not go there at all?” Ruan the Fifth said, “So you do not know what lies behind it, Professor. Let me explain.” Wu Yong said, “Indeed, I do not understand.” Ruan the Seventh immediately continued, “It is hard to tell the whole story of the Liangshan Marsh. A new band of outlaws has occupied the marsh, and they allow no one to fish there.” Wu Yong said, “I had no idea outlaws had appeared there. I have heard nothing of it here.”

p.src: Ruan the Second said, “The leader of those outlaws is a failed provincial examination candidate called Wang Lun, the ‘Scholar in White.’ The second is Du Qian, ‘Touching the Sky,’ and the third is Song Wan, the ‘Vajra in the Clouds.’ Beneath them is Zhu Gui, the ‘Dry-Land Crocodile,’ who now keeps an inn at the Lijia Crossing solely to gather information, though he is of little consequence. A new hero has lately joined them: an instructor of the Imperial Guards from the Eastern Capital, some fellow named Lin Chong, the ‘Panther Head.’ His martial skill is superb. Those scoundrels have gathered five or seven hundred men. They raid homes, plunder property, and rob and abduct passing travelers. We have not fished there for over a year. Now they guard the marsh and have cut off our livelihood; that is why the whole matter is so hard to tell.” Wu Yong said, “I truly knew nothing of this. Why have the authorities not come to arrest them?” Ruan the Fifth said, “Nowadays, whenever the authorities stir themselves anywhere, it is the common people who suffer. The moment word comes that they are entering a village, they first devour every pig, sheep, chicken, and goose raised by decent families, then demand travel money before they leave. Now they have finally met people who can deal with them! How would the officers charged with catching bandits dare come down into the villages? Even when their superiors send them out to make arrests, they are so terrified they wet and soil themselves. How could they dare look those men in the eye?” Ruan the Second said, “Though I can no longer catch large fish, at least I have been spared a good many levies and exactions.” Wu Yong said, “If that is so, those fellows must lead a merry life!” Ruan the Fifth said, “They fear neither Heaven nor Earth nor the authorities. They divide gold and silver by the scales, dress in fine silks and brocades, drink wine by the jar, and eat meat in great hunks. How could they not be merry? We three brothers possess all these abilities, yet how could we ever learn to live as they do?” Hearing this, Wu Yong rejoiced inwardly. “Now is the perfect time to use my scheme.” Ruan the Seventh said, “A man lives but one lifetime, as grass flourishes for only one autumn. We do nothing but fish for a living; if only we could live as they do for a single day!”

p.src: Wu Yong said, “Why would you want to imitate men like that? Their deeds are crimes punishable by fifty or seventy strokes of the rod, if not worse; you would merely throw away all the tigerish prowess you possess. If the authorities should arrest you, you would have brought the punishment upon yourselves.” Ruan the Second said, “The officials in charge nowadays cannot tell right from wrong; everything is in utter confusion. Countless men who have committed crimes reaching to Heaven suffer no consequences at all! We brothers cannot live merrily, but if someone were willing to take us under his wing, we would go with him.” Ruan the Fifth said, “I often think the same. It is not as though the abilities of us three brothers are inferior to anyone else’s! But who is there to recognize our worth?” Wu Yong said, “Suppose someone did recognize your worth—how could you be willing to follow him?” Ruan the Seventh said, “If someone recognizes our worth, we will go through water for him and through fire for him. If we can enjoy life for even one day, we will die with open brows and clear eyes, without regret.” Wu Yong rejoiced secretly. “All three are willing. I shall draw them in little by little.” Wu Yong urged the three of them to drink another two rounds. Truly:

p.src: Wu Yong then said, “Would you three dare go up to the Liangshan Marsh and capture those bandits?” Ruan the Seventh said, “Even if we captured them, where would we go to claim a reward? The heroes of the rivers and lakes would only laugh at us!” Wu Yong said, “My thinking was shallow. But if you resent being unable to fish, would it not be well to go there and seek a place among them?” Ruan the Second said, “Sir, you do not understand. We brothers have discussed joining them several times, but we heard all Wang Lun the ‘Scholar in White’s’ men say that he is narrow-minded and cannot tolerate men of ability. When Lin Chong from the Eastern Capital went up the mountain before, Wang Lun made things unbearably difficult for him. That fellow Wang Lun will not admit people readily. Seeing how things stood, we brothers all lost the desire to go.” Ruan the Seventh said, “If they were as generous as you, elder brother, and valued us brothers, that would be fine!” Ruan the Fifth said, “If Wang Lun showed us the same friendship that you do, Professor, we would have joined him long ago and not waited until today! We three brothers would even gladly die for him!” Wu Yong said, “A trifling man like me is hardly worth mentioning! How many heroes and gallant men there are today throughout Shandong and Hebei!” Ruan the Second said, “There may be heroes aplenty, but we brothers have never met one.”

p.src: Wu Yong said, “Do you know Chao Gai, the village head of East Creek Village here in Yuncheng County?” Ruan Xiaowu said, “Do you mean Chao Gai, the man called the Pagoda-Lifting Heavenly King?” Wu Yong said, “The very man.” Ruan Xiaoqi said, “Though he lives only a hundred-odd li from us, fate has not favored us. We know his name but have never met him.” Wu Yong said, “How can you not meet so fine a man, generous with his wealth and devoted to justice?” Ruan Xiao’er said, “We brothers have never had any business there, so we have had no chance to meet him.” Wu Yong said, “For the past few years I have been teaching at a village school near Headman Chao’s manor; now I have learned that a fortune is coming his way. I came especially to discuss it with you: what if we intercept it on the road and take it?” Ruan Xiaowu said, “That would never do. Since he is a good man who upholds justice and freely shares his wealth, if we ruined his enterprise, the heroes of the rivers and lakes would laugh at us when they heard of it.” Wu Yong said, “I thought you brothers might lack resolve, but you truly do cherish worthy men and prize righteousness. I shall tell you the truth. If you genuinely wish to help, I will let you into the affair. I am presently staying at Headman Chao’s manor. Having heard of the great names of you three, the headman specially sent me to invite you for a talk.” Ruan Xiao’er said, “We three brothers are utterly sincere, without the least falsehood! Might Headman Chao have some grand private venture in mind and mean to give us a hand up? That must be why he troubled you to come. If that truly is the case, and we three shrink from risking our lives to help him, then by this leftover wine we swear: may disaster strike us all, may foul diseases seize us, and may we die untimely deaths!” Ruan Xiaowu and Ruan Xiaoqi slapped their hands against their necks and cried, “The hot blood in these veins need only be sold to one who knows its worth!”

p.src: Wu Yong said, “You three brothers are all here. I have not come with evil intent to lure you into a trap; this is an undertaking of no small consequence! The present Grand Preceptor Cai at court has his birthday on the fifteenth day of the sixth month. His son-in-law, Secretariat Director Liang of Daming Prefecture in the Northern Capital, is now dispatching a hundred thousand strings’ worth of gold, pearls, and treasures to celebrate his father-in-law’s birthday. A good man surnamed Liu and named Tang came especially to bring us word. We now wish to invite you to confer with us, gather several good men, and seize this fortune of ill-gotten wealth at some secluded hollow in the hills, so that all of us may enjoy comfort for the rest of our lives. That is why he specially had me pretend to come buying fish, so that I might invite you three to deliberate and bring this affair to fruition. What do you think?” When Ruan Xiaowu heard this, he said, “Enough! Enough!” Then he cried, “Seventh Brother, what was it I told you!” Ruan Xiaoqi sprang to his feet and said, “The hope of a lifetime is fulfilled today! This scratches me exactly where I itch! When do we leave?” Wu Yong said, “Please set out at once, all three of you. Tomorrow at the fifth watch, we shall go together to the manor of Heavenly King Chao.” The three Ruan brothers were overjoyed. A poem bears witness: Could the learned scholar, versed in books, be one who loved wealth? The Ruan lads, too, found carefree joy in fishing! Only because the unrighteous gold and pearls were sent did all those heroes gather in the name of justice.

p.src: They passed the night there. Early the next morning, after breakfast, the three Ruan brothers gave instructions at home and followed Scholar Wu. The four left Stone Tablet Village, lengthened their stride, and took the road to East Creek Village. After traveling all day, they soon came in sight of the Chao family manor. Beneath a green locust tree in the distance stood Chao Gai and Liu Tang waiting. When they saw Wu Yong leading the three Ruan brothers straight to the tree, the two parties exchanged greetings. Chao Gai rejoiced and said, “The fame of the three Ruan heroes is no empty thing. Please come into the manor, and we shall talk.”

p.src: All six entered from outside the manor and went to the rear hall, where host and guests took their appointed seats. Wu Yong recounted their earlier conversation. Chao Gai was delighted and at once ordered his retainers to slaughter pigs and sheep and prepare for the burning of sacrificial paper. The three Ruan brothers saw that Chao Gai was imposing in appearance and frank and easy in speech. They said, “We have always loved making the acquaintance of good men, and here was one so close at hand. Had Instructor Wu not brought us together today, how could we ever have met?” The three brothers were exceedingly pleased. That evening they ate a meal and talked until midnight.

p.src: At daybreak the next morning, they laid out coins, paper horses, incense, flowers, lamps, and candles before the rear hall, set out the pigs and sheep cooked the night before, and prepared to burn sacrificial paper. Seeing Chao Gai’s deep sincerity, all were delighted, and each swore an oath: “Secretariat Director Liang oppresses the people in the Northern Capital and extorts their wealth, then sends it to the Eastern Capital to celebrate Grand Preceptor Cai’s birthday. Such wealth is truly ill-gotten. If any of us six harbors a selfish design, may Heaven and Earth destroy him, and may the gods bear witness.” When all six had sworn, they burned the paper money.

p.src: As the six resourceful heroes were drinking the sacrificial wine in the rear hall, a manor servant came to report, “There is a gentleman at the gate who wishes to see the headman and solicit alms of grain.” Chao Gai said, “You truly have no sense! You can see that I am here entertaining guests over wine. Just give him three or five sheng of rice. Why come all the way in to ask me?” The servant said, “Your humble servant offered him rice, but he would not take it. He insists on seeing the headman in person.” Chao Gai said, “He must think it too little! Go and give him another two or three dou of rice. Tell him that the headman is entertaining guests with wine at the manor today and has no time to see him.” The servant went away. After a long while he returned and said, “That gentleman would not leave even after we gave him three dou of rice. He calls himself the Daoist Yiqing and says he has come neither for money nor rice, but asks only to see the headman once.” Chao Gai said, “You fool, you do not know how to answer him. Tell him I truly have no time today, and ask him to come another day, when we may meet over tea.” The servant said, “Your humble servant told him exactly that, but the gentleman said, ‘I have not come to beg money, rice, or alms of grain. I have heard that the headman is a righteous man, and I specially ask to meet him once.’” Chao Gai said, “You keep pestering me like this and do nothing to ease my burdens! If he still thinks it too little, give him another three or four dou. Why must you come back and tell me again? If I were not drinking with my guests, I would go meet him. What difficulty would there be in that? Go and send him away, and do not come back to speak of it again!”

p.src: The gentleman struck away at him, saying all the while, “You cannot recognize a good man when you see one.” Seeing this, Chao Gai called out, “Sir, calm your anger. You came seeking Constable Chao surely for no more than alms of food. He has already given you rice, so why are you so enraged?” The gentleman laughed heartily. “This poor Taoist did not come for wine, food, money, or rice. A hundred thousand strings of cash are a trifle in my eyes. I came expressly to seek the constable because I have something to tell him. But that boorish villager was intolerably rude and reviled me, so I lost my temper.” Chao Gai asked, “Have you ever met Constable Chao?” The gentleman replied, “I have only heard his name; I have never met him.” Chao Gai said, “I am he. What is it you wish to say, sir?” The gentleman looked at him and said, “Pray do not take offense, Constable. u.src: The gentleman struck away at him, saying all the while, “You cannot recognize a good man when you see one.”
Seeing this, Chao Gai called out, “Sir, calm your anger. You came seeking Constable Chao surely for no more than alms of food. He has already given you rice, so why are you so enraged?”
The gentleman laughed heartily. “This poor Taoist did not come for wine, food, money, or rice. A hundred thousand strings of cash are a trifle in my eyes.
I came expressly to seek the constable because I have something to tell him.
But that boorish villager was intolerably rude and reviled me, so I lost my temper.”
Chao Gai asked, “Have you ever met Constable Chao?”
The gentleman replied, “I have only heard his name; I have never met him.”
Chao Gai said, “I am he.
What is it you wish to say, sir?”
The gentleman looked at him and said, “Pray do not take offense, Constable. This poor Taoist offers his respects.”

p.src: The two entered the manor. When Wu Yong saw the gentleman coming in, he slipped away together with Liu Tang and the three Ruan brothers. Now Chao Gai invited the gentleman into the rear hall and served him tea. When they had finished, the gentleman said, “This is no place for our conversation. Is there somewhere else we might sit?” At this, Chao Gai led the gentleman to a small private chamber, where host and guest took their appointed seats. Chao Gai said, “May I venture to ask your honorable surname, sir? And where is your native place?” The gentleman replied, “This poor Taoist bears the compound surname Gongsun and the given name Sheng. My Taoist name is Master Yiqing. I am a native of Jizhou. From childhood I delighted in practicing spear and staff in my village and mastered many kinds of martial arts, so people simply called me Gongsun Sheng the Elder. Later I learned a school of Taoist arts and gained the power to summon wind and rain, ride the mists, and soar upon the clouds. Throughout the rivers and lakes, they call me the ‘Dragon in the Clouds.’ I have long heard the great name of Constable Chao of Dongxi Village in Yuncheng County, but until now have had no opportunity to pay my respects. Now there are gold, pearls, and precious treasures worth a hundred thousand strings, which I mean especially to present to you as my introductory gift. I wonder whether a righteous man such as yourself will accept them?” Chao Gai laughed aloud. “Can what you speak of be the Birthday Gifts coming from the north?” The gentleman was greatly startled. “How did you know, Constable?” Chao Gai said, “It was merely a wild guess. I do not know whether it accords with your intentions.” Gongsun Sheng said, “Such a chance for wealth and rank must not be missed. The ancients said, ‘If you fail to take what should be taken, do not regret it afterward.’ What does Constable Chao think?”
